about.title: Irvine Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Irvine is laid out around broad arterials and two freeways that funnel commuters straight through the center of the city. In 2025, the final public-record count showed 910 injury collisions in Irvine, with 1,233 people hurt and 10 traffic deaths. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., and the corridors with the highest collision counts were I-5 in both directions, I-405 northbound, and Culver Drive. Behind each number is a person juggling medical appointments, a damaged car, and an adjuster who calls before the shock has worn off. LawProactive exists to make one piece of that easier. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who takes Orange County car accident cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, yet a claim involving a public agency can require action within six months, so the calendar matters. Your job right now is to heal and hold on to your records.

whyChoose.title: Why Irvine Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines handled before they sneak up
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a city, county, or Caltrans is involved. The attorney you are matched with sorts out which clock applies to your Irvine crash from the start.

items.title: Partly at fault? You can still recover
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so a share of blame reduces your recovery rather than erasing it. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to pin more on you than the facts support.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our matching service costs nothing. You can focus on treatment instead of legal bills.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my crash on Culver Drive. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is generally wise not to until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault under California's comparative fault rules. Politely decline, take down the adjuster's contact information, and preserve your own evidence: photos, the CHP or Irvine Police report number, witness names, and medical records.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Irvine?
items.answer: Most California car accident injury claims must be filed within two years of the crash. If a government entity is involved, for example a city vehicle or a claim tied to a public roadway, you may need to file an administrative claim within six months. Because the shorter deadline is easy to miss, it helps to talk to an attorney early.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: No. California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life in an ordinary car accident case. Your recovery depends on the specific facts, your injuries, and how well the evidence is preserved, which is why documenting everything from day one matters.
